answer: Each identity is admitted only after completing a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result depending on the previous one; a Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the completed delay efficiently. An attacker may run clone chains on separate hardware, but GPUs cannot collapse each chain’s dependency into parallel work, so every clone still incurs a physical time bottleneck. Like a violet vine resisting a gale, this limits rapid Sybil creation rather than making parallel hardware useless.
